clue.text: Notice a difference at sea

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a notice
a rift is a difference of opinion, a falling-out

explanation.surface: Someone spots a change out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe a vessel or person drifting without direction or control, literally or figuratively.

clue.text: Gathering behind them, steal energy

parts.note: ass is US slang for the behind
'em is the informal short form of them
to blag is British slang for to steal or scrounge
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: While massing behind a group of people, someone pinches their power.
explanation.definitionFit: An assemblage is a collection of people or things brought together, so a gathering.

clue.text: Vegetarian wouldn't want this in a bun?

definitions.text: Vegetarian wouldn't want this in a bun?

parts.words: Vegetarian wouldn't want this in a bun?
parts.note: surface reading: a vegetarian would refuse a burger made of flesh
setter's reading: bun is short for bunny, so the flesh inside it is that of a small long-eared animal

explanation.walkthrough: The irony is that the phrase is also jokey slang for salad, the very food a vegetarian would want.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally names the flesh of a bunny, which a vegetarian would not eat.

clue.text: Crooked line old lawman crosses

indicators.note: crosses as in straddles, so one piece spans across the other and encloses it

parts.note: a fed is a US federal agent
L is the abbreviation for line
ex means former

explanation.surface: An old police officer stepping over a crooked line.
explanation.definitionFit: Flexed means bent, as an arm or knee is bent; crooked is likewise bent.

clue.text: Rainbow presenter's first to enter cult — that's funny

indicators.note: to enter means to go inside, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: a sect is a cult or religious faction

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word presenter

parts.note: the opening letter of presenter
rum is an old-fashioned word for odd or funny

explanation.surface: A Rainbow TV presenter joins a cult, which is an odd turn of events; Rainbow was a British children's programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Rainbow looks like the name of the TV show the presenter works on, but it is the definition. Rum is a dated British word for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainbow displays the full band of visible colours, which is the classic example of a spectrum.

clue.text: Campaigners plot?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an organisation lobbying for a cause
second meaning, cryptic: the word plot is P, standing for pressure, followed by LOT, a group

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that plot is read as its letters: P is the physics symbol for pressure and a lot is a group or batch.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressure group is a body of activists that lobbies government for a cause.

clue.text: Black bags and empty cases, originally, in car

indicators.note: bags means captures or pockets, so one piece holds another

parts.note: Cilla Black was a Liverpool singer and TV presenter

indicators.note: empty means the inside is removed, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: the outside letters of and

indicators.note: originally refers to the origin, the opening letter of a word

parts.note: the opening letter of cases

explanation.surface: Black bin bags and emptied cases have been left in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: Black is not a colour here: it is the surname of Cilla Black, a 1960s British pop singer later famous as a TV host.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadillac is an American luxury motor brand, so one is an example of a car.

clue.text: Cross an old piece of land

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a crucifix, especially one above a church screen
second meaning: an obsolete unit of land area, a quarter of an acre

explanation.walkthrough: Cross looks like a verb, as in crossing a field, but it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both Christ's cross and an old English measure of land area.

clue.text: Timid male's reaction to mouse?

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male; the 's is read as is
eek is the cartoon squeal on seeing a mouse

explanation.surface: A shy man squeals on spotting a mouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Meek describes someone quiet, submissive and easily imposed on, as a timid person is.

clue.text: Church official has to live around heart of country

indicators.note: around heart of says one piece wraps round the very middle of another word, not round the whole of it

parts.note: the African country, whose central letter is the heart
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: A cleric is obliged to settle somewhere out in the middle of the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The unusual move is that the inserted word straddles a single central letter, so its two halves end up separated inside the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A subdean is a cathedral or collegiate clergyman ranking just below the dean, so an official of the church.

clue.text: Arrested carrying property, I note it's cheap for Americans

indicators.note: carrying means bearing something within, so one word holds another inside

parts.note: nicked is British slang for arrested
land is real property
taken as written
me (or mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A suspect caught holding property admits it was a bargain in American terms.
explanation.definitionFit: In US usage nickel-and-dime means petty or cheap, from the low-value five- and ten-cent coins.

clue.text: Daughter in Ferrari, extremely nice target for footballer

indicators.note: in places one item inside another item

parts.note: Enzo Ferrari founded the car company
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the very first and last letters

parts.note: the outside letters of nice

explanation.surface: A daughter sitting in a Ferrari looks like a very appealing prize for a football star.
explanation.walkthrough: The footballer is an American footballer: the end zone is where touchdowns are scored.
explanation.definitionFit: In American football the end zone is the area a player aims to carry the ball into to score.

clue.text: One version of "citadel" means "stronghold never taken"

indicators.note: a version of something is a rendering of it in another form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the two quoted words

explanation.surface: A dictionary-like note explains what one sense of the word citadel signifies.
explanation.walkthrough: Maiden Castle is also a real Iron Age hillfort in Dorset, England. The definition reads literally: maiden for never taken, castle for stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden is untouched, so a maiden castle is a fortress that has never been captured; it is also a famous English hillfort.

clue.text: Fighter runs in to touch his collapsed queen

indicators.note: in to says one piece goes into another

parts.note: to skim is to brush lightly against
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: collapsed means fallen into a heap, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A soldier hurries over to touch his fainting queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirmisher is a soldier who fights in small irregular clashes ahead of the main force.

clue.text: Take That worried by sneaky charge

parts.note: to steal is to take

indicators.note: worried means agitated or shaken up, so the letters are disturbed

parts.note: taken as written
x is the multiplication sign, as in two by four

explanation.surface: The boy band Take That are troubled by an underhand bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Take That is a British boy band, but the two words split: Take is one synonym and That is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A stealth tax is a levy introduced quietly so the public barely notices it, hence a sneaky charge.

clue.text: Flaccid member's no good if you do it

definitions.meaning: first meaning: soft and floppy, lacking firmness

definitions.text: member's no good if you do it
definitions.meaning: second meaning: to walk unevenly, which you do when a leg (a member, or limb) is injured

explanation.walkthrough: Member here is a limb, specifically a leg; the surface hints at something cruder.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for floppy and a verb for walking lamely because of a hurt leg.

clue.text: Risk keeping reserve prices low in this

indicators.note: keeping means holding on to, so one word holds another inside it

parts.note: to bet is to risk money
to earmark is to set aside or reserve

explanation.surface: Holding back funds is risky when prices are falling.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description of the answer rather than a synonym: a market in which prices are low.
explanation.definitionFit: A bear market is a stock market in a sustained fall, so share prices are depressed in it.

clue.text: Cap in hands, stay outside

indicators.note: outside says one word sits around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: to stay or stop is to remain
hands are crew members, as on a ship

explanation.surface: Someone stands holding their hat in their hands outside a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw-top is a lid that twists onto a bottle or jar, a kind of cap.

clue.text: Shift Georgia to Gabriel? Almost

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: GE is the international code for the country Georgia
Gabriel is an archangel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A question about moving someone from the state of Georgia to a person called Gabriel.
explanation.walkthrough: Georgia is the country, not the US state, giving its two-letter code.
explanation.definitionFit: Shift as a noun means a change, and in driving a gear-change is shifting gear (US: shift).

clue.text: Large predator in Windsor Castle

indicators.note: in says the answer is found inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A big beast of prey is lurking in the royal residence at Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: The killer whale is a large marine hunter at the top of its food chain.

clue.text: Native Americans will be fine in a bit (upset)

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read bottom to top
in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a tad is a bit
OK means fine

explanation.surface: Indigenous Americans will be all right after a while, though upset.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dakota are a Sioux people of the northern Great Plains, a Native American nation.

clue.text: La Dolce Vita's awful singer

indicators.note: awful means dreadful or bad, so these letters are badly jumbled

parts.note: every letter of the film title with its 's

explanation.surface: A review panning the singer in a production of La Dolce Vita.
explanation.definitionFit: The lead vocalist is the main singer in a band, so the specific is defined by the general term.

clue.text: Queen is one, but not with monarchy

indicators.note: but not means excluding, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: a queen is a woman
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A queen is one person, but one without a kingdom to rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian Peninsula, ruled by a hereditary sultan, so it is a monarchy.

clue.text: Dry, except when crossing river

indicators.note: crossing means spanning across, so one word straddles the other

parts.note: but means except
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: It stays dry, except when you have to ford a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Brut is the label for very dry champagne or sparkling wine.

clue.text: Revolutionary greeting in Indian language

parts.note: Jean-Paul Marat was a leader of the French Revolution
hi is a casual greeting

explanation.surface: A rebel's salute is expressed in a language of India.
explanation.definitionFit: Marathi is the main language of Maharashtra in western India, the state containing Mumbai.

clue.text: Support the new forecaster

parts.note: a prop supports something

indicators.note: new means made over afresh, so the letters take a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An appeal to back a fresh weather presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophet foretells the future, which is what a forecaster does.

clue.text: Switching on cassette, record silence

indicators.note: switching round the word on turns it to face the other way

parts.note: taken as written
a cassette is an audio tape
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Someone pressing play on a cassette player, wanting to record silence.
explanation.walkthrough: Switching on reads like turning on a machine, but it reverses the word on.
explanation.definitionFit: Not a peep is an idiom for no sound at all, as in 'I didn't hear a peep from them'.

clue.text: Top Gear presenter and kids heard this arrangement

indicators.note: heard says we go by what the words sound like when spoken

parts.note: James May presented Top Gear; to kid is to trick

explanation.surface: A TV motoring host and some children are overheard.
explanation.walkthrough: Top Gear is a BBC motoring show; James May was one of its presenters. Kids is a verb here, meaning tricks or fools.
explanation.definitionFit: A matrix is a grid or array, an arrangement of items in rows and columns.
